why_trail.why: Context is loaded and the floor is my own measurement rather than the handoff's. The three blockers are understood as one substantive code defect (B2, selection by dict order at decide_session_start) plus two instrument/prose defects (B1, B3), the second of which the B2 fix partly discharges.

The reviewer's six cases are now executable tests rather than a scratch script. Two constructions matter: both spines sit outside _scan_active_spine's glob and that emptiness is asserted, so a green cannot be the blind scan answering by luck; and the withhold case is scoped to what the binding can hand out, because a session owning nothing still falls through to the scan (tc1), which is out of this gate's reach.

B2 fixed by extracting _own_entries(candidates, owners, own_key) -- the subset the acting agent owns -- and calling it at BOTH sites, which is the reviewer's Fowler extraction in the shape that fits: the two sites' candidate sequences differ only in what rides along after element [0], so the comparison genuinely is one function, while the FALLBACKS stay separate on purpose (decide_stop must still render something because the stop blocks regardless; decide_session_start hands out nothing). Collateral, and it needs the Commander's eye: two pre-existing tests (test_session_start_resumes_from_a_spine_bound_only_under_a_composite_key and test_session_start_composite_key_entry_still_renders_full_imperative_unchanged) asserted that a bare SessionStart resumes from a SUBAGENT's composite-key entry -- the reviewer's case 3 in same-tree form. They and the B2 fix cannot both stand. Rewritten to the new rule, keeping #419's read-through asserted directly and adding the round trip that shows the entry is still reachable by the agent that owns it.

B3 is discharged by the B2 fix plus a header that now states the shared rule instead of asserting a property one site did not have. The lane's lesson applied to my own prose as well as the inherited prose: six sentences failed the read-whole test, two of them mine.

B1 fixed at the root rather than at the symptom: BASE_REV is pinned to the gate's base 999b7663 (never rev-parse HEAD), a third arm carries the BLOCKED intermediate e3e50a69, and _assert_arms_are_what_they_claim identifies each arm by symbols the changes moved -- BEFORE has _foreign_worktree only, BLOCKED has _is_own_entry but not _own_entries, AFTER has both -- plus pairwise byte-difference. The guard was DEMONSTRATED to fail, not asserted: repointing BASE_REV at e3e50a69 and BLOCKED_REV at 999b7663 each kill the run with named reasons and exit 1. The three-arm table now shows the regression and its repair in one place: S9 BLOCKED injects CREW-MARKER where AFTER injects PARENT-MARKER; S11 BLOCKED injects CREW-MARKER where AFTER injects nothing; S12 BLOCKED answers agent A where AFTER answers the agent the payload names; S1-S8 are identical BLOCKED vs AFTER, so the Stop path did not move.

Suite green at 3183 passed / 5 skipped / 0 failed, cache cleared and env scrubbed, up +6 from my own 3177 floor -- and the +6 accounts for every test: 6 new methods in OwnershipIsBindingKeyNotWorktree (8 -> 14), 2 tests renamed and rewritten in place (net zero), no deletions. Subtests +12 (2 write-order + 4 withhold + 6 inert-location). Failure distribution derived mechanically on BOTH sides, 0 FAILED lines each. map/INDEX.md regenerated with py -m scripts.code_map build, never hand-edited: scripts 1224 -> 1225 (_own_entries), tests 4843 -> 4850.

Result artifact written to the handoff's named path -- that write is the delivery. It carries the three blocker fixes, the extract-vs-duplicate call with its reasoning, the two rewritten pre-existing tests surfaced as the decision the Commander may want to reverse (one line if so), my read on the decision formulation, and the recorded refusal of the parent-spine Stop hook.
